title.en: Moon phases from an observer viewpoint

summary: Link an external Sun-Earth-Moon diagram with the lunar disk seen by an Earth observer.
objective: Show the Moon phase from Earth alongside a 3D orbital view, keeping the sunlit side physically consistent.
intent_signals: Show the Moon phase from Earth alongside a 3D orbital view, keeping the sunlit side physically consistent.
Link an external Sun-Earth-Moon diagram with the lunar disk seen by an Earth observer.
example_prompts: Show the Moon phase from Earth alongside a 3D orbital view, keeping the sunlit side physically consistent.
Create an explorable 3D explanation of Moon phases with observer disk.
negative_signals: No lunar ephemeris, libration, topographic shadow detail or eclipse prediction; the observer disk uses a distant-observer approximation, not the perspective cap seen from an exaggerated nearby sphere.
not_for: No lunar ephemeris, libration, topographic shadow detail or eclipse prediction; the observer disk uses a distant-observer approximation, not the perspective cap seen from an exaggerated nearby sphere.

entities.name: Earth and Moon markers
entities.guidance: Build separate spheres with exaggerated sizes and an explicit orbit plane; use a fixed observer marker on or near Earth with a declared camera convention.

entities.name: Sunlight geometry
entities.guidance: Show parallel incoming-light arrows and a Sun-direction marker outside the model; illuminate the Moon hemisphere facing that direction.

entities.name: Observer disk
entities.guidance: Render an orthographic second view of the lunar sphere along the observer-to-Moon-center direction, labeled with phase angle and illuminated fraction. Keep exaggerated overview distances out of this disk projection.

state_contract.model: Schematic Sun direction, Earth observer and Moon center determine the phase angle alpha=Sun-Moon-observer. Use parallel illumination and an orthographic disk viewed along the observer-to-Moon-center direction; its illuminated fraction=(1+cos(alpha))/2. This is the distant-observer projection approximation.
state_contract.authority: The same light direction and observer position determine both the external hemisphere shading and observer-camera disk; phase names are derived from declared orbital direction.
actions: Switch between external and observer view.
Compare quarter, full and new configurations.
Reset orbital direction and camera convention.

invariants: A quarter phase shows about half the apparent disk illuminated, not a quarter of it.
Phase shading follows Sun direction rather than the external camera.
At full phase the observer-facing hemisphere is illuminated; at new phase it is mostly dark in the ideal model.
motion_guidance: Advance the declared orbit angle smoothly; do not change light direction to paint a desired phase.
Keep Earth shadows disabled or outside the phase-only model and explain that eclipses are a separate alignment phenomenon.
known_limits: No lunar ephemeris, libration, topographic shadow detail or eclipse prediction; the observer disk uses a distant-observer approximation, not the perspective cap seen from an exaggerated nearby sphere.
A coplanar schematic must not imply an eclipse every new and full Moon; phase and eclipse mechanisms are separate.
Curated recipe only; no runtime scene or rendered behavior has been verified for this record.

claims.statement: Lunar phases arise because an Earth observer sees different portions of the Moon sunlit hemisphere as it orbits.
claims.scope: Reflected-sunlight geometry, distinct from the Earth shadow during lunar eclipses.

source_refs.locator: Why the Moon has phases; phase descriptions

object_craft.structure: Build separate spheres with exaggerated sizes and an explicit orbit plane; use a fixed observer marker on or near Earth with a declared camera convention.
object_craft.material: Diffuse lunar sphere and controlled illumination; avoid ambient fill that makes the unlit fraction look self-luminous.
